title: Hyperbole
body:
Another day
-one of the few, to tell the truth,
yet getting more and more frequent-
where we won't have exchanged a word
-not a sweet and tender one
like once upon a time
in that earlier season-
just a simple word

Where the phone won't have rung
not even once
with you on the other end
asking me how I am
-how I feel, that is, and how I spent today;
I want so badly to hope that
at least for now
you haven't yet forgotten my
face-

Where you won't have sent
an old photo of ours
in a text message
-you used to do that once;
That's how you declared your "presence"
and your "I'm thinking of you"
"I'm thinking of US"

"I love you."

And somehow like this evening will fall
and another night will have arrived
-one of the frequent ones, to tell the truth,
and getting more and more numerous lately-
where I will lie down
by myself on the
floor
flat on my back
-not on the double mattress;
on the floor.
The mattress is too big and doesn't
suit
my loneliness-

Where I'll be staring at the ceiling
And the chandelier
-not the stars on a beach by the waves
like we used to-

Where I'll be listening only to my silence
-I won't have any thoughts to make;
Better that way! They torment me so much lately-

And I'll hear the footsteps
of the dog
belonging to the neighbor on the second floor

-he at least made peace with his solitude
and chose
the only certain
loyal friend to make it
tolerable-

Midnight.
And early tomorrow morning the wake-up call

Before I fall asleep
if I make the decision to call first myself
you'll probably have it turned off
pretending it ran out of battery.

But if I'm lucky and you pick up
then I'll come face to face with a
sorrowful
coldness
-frequent, very frequent, lately-
a feeling expressed, perhaps
in the most authentic way
and sterilized
of any displays of passion you used to have.

And if this
complaint of mine
we end up discussing
then you'll tell me that I'm exaggerating

So be it.
Let me be exaggerating.
That is a good sign of love
which happens to be (as it should)
the source of my exaggeration
and of the cunning thought (of fear)
that your own love has run dry.

And what, then, wouldn't I give for you to
exaggerate
too, once again
for a little while
I would rejoice in it so much.

Perhaps then
I wouldn't have any complaint to hold against you.
